To find the stationary points of y = f(x), you first need to find the derivative of the function, f'(x). Set the derivative equal to zero and solve for x. These solutions are the x-coordinates of the stationary points. To determine if they are maxima, minima, or points of inflection, you can use the second derivative test or analyze the sign of the first derivative around the points.
replies.Briefly, how do you perform a Principal: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is a technique used to reduce the dimensionality of data. You start by standardizing the data, then compute the covariance matrix. Next, you find the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of this matrix. The eigenvectors with the highest eigenvalues are the principal components. You can then project the data onto these components. The mathematics can be complex, but there are many tools and software that can help you perform PCA without needing to understand all the details. Don't get anxious; focus on the concepts and tools available.
